correctness.rationale: For an odd \(y\), write \(y+3=2^j k\) with odd \(k\); the next odd state is \(ky\). If \(k=1\) this gives a primitive cycle. For odd \(k\ge3\), a terminal arrival would imply \(2^j(k^2-2^{2h})=3(k-1)\) with \(h\ge1\) and \(2^h<k\). But the left side is at least \(4k-2>3(k-1)\), contradiction. Every nonterminal odd state grows by at least a factor of three; intermediate even iterates are no smaller than the following odd one. Exact unique odd-part counting gives the summatory formula. The finite verifier corroborates but is not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The finding completely classifies every positive initial state for the natural plus-three quadratic member adjacent to recently published plus-one/minus-one Collatz-type dynamics, including primitive periods, basins, divergence and a precise bounded-initial-value count. Unlike the plus-one map with exceptional preperiodic odd part \(5\), the plus-three rule has no exceptional bounded starts. The infinite classification is mathematically motivated by the neighboring published open-family direction.
